DeepWalk does not incorporate a node attribute feature matrix X directly into the SkipGram hierarchical softmax tree during the unsupervised random walk phase. In the original DeepWalk formulation, the algorithm first generates truncated random walks over the graph, treats the resulting node sequences as sentences, and then trains SkipGram with hierarchical softmax to predict context nodes from a target node. The hierarchical softmax tree is built over the vocabulary of nodes, not over node attributes, so X is not used as a direct input to the tree construction or the random-walk objective.

If a node attribute matrix X is available, it can be used only in an extended or hybrid model, for example by concatenating attributes with learned embeddings, initializing embeddings from features, or replacing the pure node-vocabulary representation with a feature-aware encoder. Those are not part of the original DeepWalk method. DeepWalk’s core contribution is to learn low-dimensional node representations from random-walk co-occurrence statistics, preserving network neighborhoods rather than explicitly modeling node attributes.

So the direct answer is: it does not. DeepWalk uses random walks plus SkipGram hierarchical softmax on node IDs, and any use of X would require a modification beyond the original algorithm.
confidence_reasoning: The original DeepWalk method is well-established: it uses truncated random walks and SkipGram with hierarchical softmax over node IDs, not direct node-attribute injection into the tree.
